an4.123:1.1: “Bhikkhus, these four individuals are found in the world.
an4.123:1.3: Take an individual who, fully withdrawn from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and dwells in the first stage of meditation, which has the delight and contentment born of seclusion, with thinking and considering.
an4.123:1.4: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.
an4.123:1.5: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.
an4.123:1.6: The lifespan of the gods of the Divinity’s host is one eon.
an4.123:1.7: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.
an4.123:1.8: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.
an4.123:1.9: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.
an4.123:2.1: Furthermore, take an individual who, as thinking and considering are stilled, enters and dwells in the second stage of meditation, which has the delight and contentment born of concentration, with internal clarity and poise, without thinking and considering.
an4.123:2.2: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.
an4.123:2.3: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of streaming radiance.
an4.123:2.4: The lifespan of the gods of streaming radiance is two eons.
an4.123:2.5: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.
an4.123:2.6: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.
an4.123:2.7: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.
an4.123:3.1: Furthermore, take an individual who, with the fading away of delight, enters and dwells in the third stage of meditation, where they meditate with equanimity, with awareness and comprehension, personally experiencing the contentment of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and aware, one meditates content.’
an4.123:3.2: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.
an4.123:3.3: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of universal beauty.
an4.123:3.4: The lifespan of the gods of universal beauty is four eons.
an4.123:3.5: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.
an4.123:3.6: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.
an4.123:3.7: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.
an4.123:4.1: Furthermore, take an individual who, giving up pleasure and pain, and ending former happiness and sadness, enters and dwells in the fourth stage of meditation, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and awareness.
an4.123:4.2: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.
an4.123:4.3: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of abundant fruit.
an4.123:4.4: The lifespan of the gods of abundant fruit is five hundred eons.
an4.123:4.5: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.
an4.123:4.6: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.
an4.123:4.7: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.
an4.123:4.8: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
